title: Reuse the existing activity effect for child handoff publication
evidence: mutation/activity.rs:78-83 and live/event/activity.rs:17-22 hold the same head, source, deletion-key vector and optional entry.
HandoffRecords::contribute at activity.rs:233-263 is the same concrete family/key/write sequence as ActivityEffect::contribute at live/event/activity.rs:351-381.
proposal: Return ActivityEffect from the handoff preparation path and expose its constructor or fields only within crate::mutation. Delete HandoffRecords and its duplicate writer. Keep the handoff-specific source, final-answer, selected-path and retention admission unchanged.
required_contract_changes: None. Prepared effect representation is internal; durable records, reservations and write order remain unchanged.

estimated_net_lines.basis: Remove a seven-line duplicate representation and approximately 32-line writer plus imports; reserve small construction/visibility adjustment. No activity derivation or retention savings counted.

verification: Run child handoff, activity lifecycle/retention/corruption and reopen tests.
Compare exact reconciliation record families and contribution write order before and after.

title: Share next-item admission and selected-history effects for freeze and finalize
evidence: freeze.rs:34-79 and finalize.rs:21-66 repeat required thread/turn/state/summary reads and same origin, revision, terminal lifecycle, next ordinal and turn-item identity admission.
Both paths derive selected history timestamp as max(existing, request), conditionally mark selected summary incomplete, and write the same state/summary/transcript invalidation prefix.

Freeze additionally authenticates/freezes provider content and updates item/index state; finalization checks current projection and advances its own frontier. These transitions are not interchangeable.
proposal: Introduce one typed next-item admission result and pure selected-summary update helper, then reuse the small common contribution prefix. Leave freeze content authentication, finalization projection admission, selected-path lookup placement and each caller's invalidation order explicit.
required_contract_changes: None. Preserve first failing read/error, exact state revision and ordinal fences, selected-path-only summary changes, and visible-and-selected transcript invalidation.

estimated_net_lines.basis: Approximately 45-55 admission lines, 18 summary lines and 25 writer-prefix lines duplicated; subtract typed result/signature/call-site glue and focused regression adjustment. No provider lifecycle or transcript builder simplification counted.

verification: Run live history replay/finalization, pending-tail, canonical-finalization and mutation fault tests.
Check off-selected-path and invisible item behavior, current versus stale projection rejection, revision/ordinal conflict ordering and freeze/finalize read failures.

Take the text block once around a bounded flush loop and restore it once; share the final text-output helper while retaining variant-specific block kind and EOF behavior. Verify byte-identical IDs/digests/checkpoints and output sequence after resume at each bounded parser checkpoint.

evidence: advance.rs:13-26 stores three separate record vectors and three parallel presence vectors; preparation fills these after exact occupied-record checks and contribution zips them again.
next_build, set and head are three Options but finish creates exactly a continuation build or a completed set/head pair; contribution dynamically checks the already-established pairing.

Preserve independent resource and resource-index existence flags. Return a typed continuation-versus-completed effect from finish instead of three independently optional fields.
required_contract_changes: None. Keep materialization before identity reads, projection/stable-index/unstable-index/resource-index read order, independent occupied-record comparisons, reservations and contribution order. Do not replace exact record checks with a shared presence bit.

estimated_net_lines.basis: Remove duplicate presence-vector fields, initialization, transfer and nested zip/guard plumbing; reserve record/effect construction and typed enum match. No separate line savings assigned to the enum itself; benefit includes eliminating impossible prepared combinations.

verification: Run stable/volatile item projection reuse, pending-tail identity and projection fault/reconciliation tests.
Check independently missing/exact/conflicting resource and resource-index combinations plus final set/head collision and continuing parser steps.

title: Extend the first-encode narrative derivation to typed provider-frame preparation
evidence: mutation/provider_frame/prepare.rs encodes the same typed frame first through CountingSink and then through NarrativeCountingSink before later durable staging traversal.

Typed AgentMessage and Plan encoding have at most one Narrative text span; Encoder::text emits no span for empty text and exactly one whole logical span for nonempty inline or referenced text. Citation/other metadata spans do not carry the Narrative role.
The initial content hash is only known after the first encode; narrative capture therefore must retain the span's logical metadata until finalizing that digest.
proposal: During the first CountingSink traversal capture the sole narrative span for narrative-bearing item kinds, preserving role/multiplicity validation. After the first frame digest is known derive narrative append/reference/completion metadata from that capture and delete NarrativeCountingSink plus its second full encode comparison. Keep the durable stage_provider_frame traversal and all receipts/reconciliation handling.
required_contract_changes: None. Retain exact frame bytes, source offset, prior narrative append semantics, empty narrative behavior, completion mismatch comparison, chunk bounds and move-only staging custody.

estimated_net_lines.basis: Remove NarrativeCountingSink struct/new/impl (~135 lines) and second encode/reference/frontier comparison (~36 lines); retain ~45-65 lines of one-span capture, role/multiplicity validation and post-digest narrative/completion derivation plus regression adjustments. Incremental mutation-only estimate excludes existing compiler90-130. This is an extension of existing SP-003, not a second independent finding or the whole SP-003 estimate; root must add this mutation-only increment once.

verification: Compare first/subsequent AgentMessage and Plan frames, empty starts/deltas/completions, references and citation metadata.
Run provider staging/resume/fault and segmented completion-mismatch tests; require identical target metadata and encoded bytes.

title: Retain the bounded durable Markdown parser after screening pulldown-cmark
evidence: Beryl concepts.md:367-424 fixes byte-preserving block/source semantics and bounded paragraph/code/table/page limits; persisted checkpoints include carry, block state, digests and source cursors.

pulldown-cmark v0.13.4 Parser::new_with_broken_link_callback calls run_first_pass(text, options) before returning its iterator. firstpass.rs:24-40 reserves a tree proportional to input size; FirstPass::run:68-79 scans the entire supplied string.

The public Parser has private input/tree/allocation state. Its constructors, reference_definitions and into_offset_iter expose no append input, checkpoint serialization or restore entry point. serde derives apply to event/tag/value types in lib.rs, not Parser.
Offset event ranges can overlap for structural events and are not themselves Beryl's exact source-byte partition; source-backed slices and Beryl fallback/marker handling would remain necessary.
proposal: Do not replace the durable parser in this audit. A future experiment could parse already-bounded closed blocks, but must keep Beryl block recognition, source partitioning and persisted checkpoint logic and prove substantial net deletion after adapters before proposing adoption.
required_contract_changes: Direct whole-item adoption conflicts with existing bounded residency/resume and exact byte-source contracts. No contract change is proposed or authorized.

estimated_net_lines.basis: No credible substantial net reduction established. Existing parser.rs/output.rs/syntax.rs total 1057 lines include persisted state, bounded accumulation, resources and markers that this event parser does not replace; adapter cost is not hidden as savings.

verification: If revisited, independently compare byte source ranges/digests, Unicode and CRLF/bare-CR behavior, zero-width markers, threshold boundaries and interrupted fence/table checkpoint resume.
Measure peak resident memory for unbounded input and adapter line count before accepting replacement. No dependency was installed or code compiled during this audit.

dependency_candidates.name: pulldown-cmark

screened_configuration.reason: Parser API only. Default getopts/html are unnecessary; html pulls pulldown-cmark-escape. serde does not provide durable Parser state; optional SIMD is unnecessary.

maintenance_and_adoption: Version 0.13.4 release documents a TightParagraph panic fix; upstream CI exercises MSRV/stable/nightly, no-default/default/serde/SIMD modes, WASM build and DoS regression fixtures.

Official rust-lang/cargo Cargo.toml at commit 77fb9722e3e5ec33ca7adc1e99c9e15e512bb21f declares pulldown-cmark ^0.13.3 with default-features=false, features=[html]. This is ecosystem adoption evidence, not proof Cargo resolves exactly 0.13.4.
dependency_candidates.platform_assessment: Pure Rust parser; upstream README excludes optional SIMD from its no-unsafe statement and identifies SIMD as x64. Screened configuration leaves SIMD off. Inspected CI covered Ubuntu and WASM; no claim of verified native Windows behavior.
dependency_candidates.security_assessment: No pulldown-cmark package advisory path found in the complete, nontruncated official RustSec advisory-db tree at revision 5a0ebedfe8bdd2e295b171f4162f8c977bcad9a5. This bounded registry check is not a security audit or a claim that no vulnerabilities exist. Input-proportional eager first-pass tree remains the architectural concern.
dependency_candidates.adapter_cost: Must retain closed-block detection, durable fence/table counters and digests, bounded UTF-8 carry, exact source-byte partition/fallback, source cursors, stable output IDs and marker handling. Parsing closed bounded slices avoids whole-item residency but does not remove most present code; no net saving demonstrated.

evidence: All 43 source files in this cohort were inspected at full-body depth except the 16-line provider_frame module declaration root. Runtime callbacks and independent point reads enforce persisted source, target, first/last mutable anchors and exact record identity rather than redundant local shape checks.
Provider observation stream and typed PIV1 source remain different validation/representation boundaries; AC-007 normalized vocabulary deferral does not justify deleting either.
Current transcript snapshots, stable/volatile item generations, terminal finalization, historical native/recovery bindings and physical read failures have distinct authority and lifecycle semantics.
proposal: Keep the explicit bounded traversal, exact record admission, reconciliation reservations/receipts, independent validator reads and old-generation state. Apply only the narrowly identified representations and pure helper changes. Treat transcript counter cleanup as low-value follow-up with zero separate estimate; do not trade read ordering for a one-pass shortcut.
required_contract_changes: None. SQ-005 internal validation-error reuse is confirmed at mutation/provider_frame/completion.rs and live/event/item/publication.rs: physical Read stays distinct from domain-specific completion/frame rejection. All SQ savings remain counted there.

estimated_net_lines.basis: Retention and cross-cohort coordination only. PRE-004 owns all temporary-home savings, SQ-005 error-domain savings and AC-007 deferred normalized vocabulary; no additive estimate here.

verification: No source implementation, build or test was performed; this is observational audit evidence.
When implementing accepted findings, run focused default/test-faults and corruption/reopen/fault cases according to the effective persistent, shared-resource and external-input rigor contracts.
